material_findings.title: Printed execution commands still hide the actual outer exit
material_findings.counterexample: If the wrapper returns 1, or timeout returns nonzero, the requested command runs a successful trailing echo and the enclosing shell returns 0 despite printing outer_exit=1 (or the timeout code). [Request, lines 77-78](../../s5-v7/V7_SELECTIVE_PREP_REQUEST.md#L77-L78)
material_findings.consequence: The external invocation status can falsely appear successful, contradicting the request's own raw-capture qualification. [Request, lines 77-78](../../s5-v7/V7_SELECTIVE_PREP_REQUEST.md#L77-L78)
material_findings.minimal_correction: In the parent grant, guard cd and capture the timeout command in if/else immediately, record the saved status, then exit with that same status; do not use the trailing echo as the observable command result.
material_findings.nonexecuted_R1_caller_shape: bash -c 'cd /home/user/workspace/execution/op88/s5-v7 || exit 70; if S5_CTL_GRANT=granted-by-parent timeout --foreground -k 10 140 bash controls-v7-selective/run-t3-checker.sh; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi; printf "outer_exit=%s\n" "$rc"; exit "$rc"'
material_findings.qualification: Illustrative raw-status correction only, not an execution grant or a solution to A-03.

material_findings.title: Inherited run_gate registers ownership only after its interruptible startup sleep
material_findings.counterexample: Deliver TERM to the driver after the setsid child is spawned at 67-68 but while the parent is in sleep 0.2 at 69: its trap exits 143 before OWNED_PGIDS is populated, and EXIT cleanup iterates an empty list while the detached Jest child can continue. [T0 driver, lines 35,47-49 and 67-74](../../s5-v7/controls-v7-selective/ctl-t0-only.sh#L47-L74)
material_findings.related_identity_counterexample: If the spawned child has not yet performed setsid when ps runs, the sampled pgid can still be the caller group; that value is added without checking pgid==spawned_pid or excluding the caller group and later authorizes negative-group TERM/KILL. [T0 driver, lines 67-74](../../s5-v7/controls-v7-selective/ctl-t0-only.sh#L67-L74)
material_findings.consequence: The eventual T0 slot does not reliably provide the promised owned cleanup on interruption and can adopt an unowned caller group as signal authority; this is inherited from V6, not introduced by deleting T1/T2/T3. [T0 driver, lines 47-49 and 69-76](../../s5-v7/controls-v7-selective/ctl-t0-only.sh#L47-L76) [Exact selector diff](../../s5-v7/controls-v6-to-v7-t0-only.diff)
material_findings.minimal_correction: Before granting R2 execution, freeze a bounded startup-publication/adoption correction: register the spawned child immediately, resolve interruption safely through verified session/group identity, never authorize caller-group signals, and retain truthful nonzero recovery on uncertainty.
material_findings.requested_future_discriminator: Deterministic interruption between spawn and identity registration, plus delayed session creation with a caller-group decoy; prove no unowned signal and no unaccounted owned child.
material_findings.scope_limit: No new product/spec/harness changes or broad supervisor rewrite requested; source restoration can proceed independently.

material_findings.title: 120-second internal and 140-second outer completion claims omit explicit kill/cleanup grace
material_findings.R1_counterexample: With six aggregate seconds remaining, invoke permits a six-second timeout plus its explicit five-second kill-after interval, so that call can already run to elapsed 125 rather than 120 before wrapper logging; the outer requested 140-second timeout also has a ten-second kill-after interval. [Checker wrapper, lines 40-44](../../s5-v7/controls-v7-selective/run-t3-checker.sh#L40-L44) [Request, line 77](../../s5-v7/V7_SELECTIVE_PREP_REQUEST.md#L77)
material_findings.R2_counterexample: With six seconds remaining, run_gate can spend those six polling seconds and then ten more in TERM grace, followed by wait, group cleanup and EXIT cleanup; none is checked against AGG_BOUND, and the requested outer wrapper allows twenty seconds beyond its 140-second initial timeout. [T0 driver, lines 47-49 and 64-76](../../s5-v7/controls-v7-selective/ctl-t0-only.sh#L64-L76) [Request, line 78](../../s5-v7/V7_SELECTIVE_PREP_REQUEST.md#L78)
material_findings.consequence: The requested <=140-second slot and internal 120-second aggregate completion are not the actual enforced end-to-end bounds; for R2, unconditional wait after KILL and A-02 mean an outer wrapper alone is not proof of detached-child cleanup. [T0 driver, lines 69-76](../../s5-v7/controls-v7-selective/ctl-t0-only.sh#L69-L76) [Request, lines 77-78](../../s5-v7/V7_SELECTIVE_PREP_REQUEST.md#L77-L78)
material_findings.minimal_correction: Before R1, correct the grant's budget terminology and reserve explicit kill/output/cleanup time, with raw timeout status and no success claim on expiry; checker and fixtures need no logic change for this correction. Before R2, include cancellation/confirmed-owned-cleanup in the successor's actual deadline and request, with no unconditional wait after unconfirmed termination.
material_findings.qualification: 140+10=150 for R1 and 140+20=160 for R2 are nominal outer timeout-plus-kill allowances, not attestations of whole descendant-tree completion; no current uutils/GNU exit-code equivalence is asserted.
